sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: The Aravidu dynasty was founded by **Tirumala Deva Raya**, brother of Rama Raya, after the fall of the Tuluva dynasty.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: The capital was shifted from the ruined **Hampi (Vijayanagara)** to **Penukonda** and later to **Chandragiri** for strategic defense.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: The period is defined by the **Nayaka System**, where provincial governors (Nayakas) became increasingly autonomous, leading to the eventual disintegration of central authority.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The empire survived for nearly 80 years post-Talikota, primarily through diplomatic maneuvering and shifting alliances with the Deccan Sultanates.

Constant conflict with Bijapur and Golconda

items.definition: A military-feudal system where land grants (Amaram) were given to military commanders (Nayakas) in exchange for maintaining troops and paying tribute to the king.
The territory assigned to a Nayaka; the holder was known as an Amaranayaka, responsible for local administration and revenue collection.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Key Application 1**: Patronage of Telugu literature and art, particularly in the courts of Raghunatha Nayaka.
• **Key Application 2**: Diplomatic engagement with European powers (Portuguese/Dutch) to secure trade and military support.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Internal rebellions by Nayakas and constant pressure from the Bijapur and Golconda Sultanates.
• **Solutions**: Attempted centralization by Venkata II, which temporarily stabilized the empire.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'S-S-T-A' (Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu).
• **Decoded Meaning**: The chronological order of the four dynasties of Vijayanagara.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Do not confuse the Aravidu dynasty with the Tuluva dynasty. Krishnadevaraya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty, NOT the Aravidu dynasty.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Political Fragmentation' to describe the Aravidu period, contrasting it with the 'Centralized Imperialism' of the Tuluva period.

keyTakeaways: Aravidu was the final dynasty, ruling from 1570 to 1646.
The shift of capital to Penukonda signifies the loss of the Tungabhadra heartland.
The rise of independent Nayaka kingdoms (Madurai, Tanjore, Ikkeri) was the defining feature of this era.
